LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Ackerspec: Requests planted fields in a suburb or rural ward. Associate a field with building categories through tags, or place it inside a district to connect it to that district. Crop lists allow several field definitions to share plant choices.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_BudgetEntry: Requests a category of buildings or one specific piece within a district. Use count for the requested quantity and filler for buildings that may occupy space left over after the main programme. Naming a piece takes precedence over tag.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_BuildableRuleDef: Assigns otherwise uncategorised buildings to architect categories when the building-aid setting is enabled. Rules match source filenames and are evaluated by rank. See [Buildability rules](Modding-Overview#buildability-rules).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_ContentZoneSpec: Configures a connected region in the older PieceDef.content grid. Its symbol identifies the region, category selects objects, and lootTable supplies their contents. New pieces can use Fill anchors instead; see [Anchors](Modding-Pieces#anchors).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_CropEintrag: Adds a plant and its relative selection weight to a CropListDef. The referenced ThingDef must be a plant; missing or invalid plants are skipped.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_CropListDef: Shares a weighted selection of plants between fields and pens. Fields and pens refer to this definition through crops; if it has no usable plants, their local plants list is used instead.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Dekospec: Places decorative or defensive pieces along a ward road network. Use it inside decor for spaced decoration or defenses for defensive positions distributed through the ward.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_DistrictSpec: Groups building requests within a ward and supplies preferences for their position. Fields, pens and mines attached to the district can be associated with its buildings. District names must be unique across the settlement, including districts in different wards.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_DungeonProfileDef: Older dungeon profile type. Dungeons now use SettlementPlanDef with kind Dungeon and a levels list instead. See [Dungeon levels](Modding-Dungeons) for the available implementation and its limitations.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_FactionFlagDef: Assigns flag object lists to a faction. Object anchors with factionFlag enabled use this assignment; without a matching flag they fall back to their own object list. See [Faction flags](Unit-Swap#faction-flags).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Garnisonseintrag: Requests defenders from a pawn list for one ward. The post determines where they stand. Without a garrison factor a ward with a garrison does not also receive the ordinary point-based defenders; with wealthFactor above 0 the shared budget also buys pawns for it. See [Garrisons](Modding-Pawns#garrisons).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Gehegespec: Requests fenced animal pens in the Rural ward. A pawn list supplies the animal species, herd sets the requested herd size, and available pen area limits the result. Plant choices can come from a crop list or the plants fallback.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_HafenEintrag: Requests a harbour piece or category and its quantity. Add this entry to HafenSpec.entries on a settlement plan.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_HafenSpec: Adds harbour buildings near a settlement when a suitable coast or sufficiently wide river is available. Entries select the buildings; range limits their distance from the settlement.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_HelpDef: Provides help text for the in-game editor. Use the documented key for the relevant help button and translated text for the content. See [Help texts](Modding-Overview#help-texts).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LegendEntry: Maps one character in a piece grid to an object, terrain, roof, pawn or anchor. The grid determines how the entry is used: an anchors symbol refers to an anchor, while a terrain symbol resolves a floor. See [The legend](Modding-Pieces#the-legend).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LegendVariant: Adds a weighted alternative to a legend entry. Alternatives are selected per cell, so repeated symbols can produce different objects or terrain. The parent entry also participates with weight 1 when it has its own object or terrain.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LootBuildingCategoryDef: Supplies the objects placed by Fill and Object anchors, such as shelves, barrels or market stalls. Members that fit the anchor area are selected by footprint size. The list can also configure occupants for enclosed containers. See [Object lists](Modding-Loot#object-lists).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LootEntry: Defines one result in a loot table: a specific item, a random item from a ThingCategoryDef, or another loot table. The enclosing list determines selection: always uses chance, while entries uses relative weight. If several result fields are set, table takes precedence over category, then thing.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LootMember:
Configures one object in an object list, including its loot override and what happens after its contents are removed. A simple member can be written as `
  • ThingDefName
    • `; use a structured entry for additional fields. See [Member nodes](Modding-Loot#member-nodes).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LootTableDef: Generates item selections for containers, shelves or loose loot. The always list is evaluated first; entries are then selected by weight. Nested tables let several containers share a common set of goods. See [Loot tables](Modding-Loot#loot-tables).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_MapStepsDef: Controls which map generation steps are suppressed or gated by tech level on CBF maps. The framework reads the definition named CBF_MapSteps, so extend that definition rather than creating another independently named one.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_MaterialListDef: Resolves named construction roles into objects, materials, terrain and roofs. Settlement plans must name a material list. Ordered candidate lists provide fallbacks when content from another mod is unavailable. See [Material lists](Material-Lists).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_MaterialRole: Defines the candidates for one construction role, optionally restricted to a ward or matching fortification pieces. Candidates are tried in order; a matching forPieces condition takes precedence over a ward condition. See [Material lists](Modding-Overview#material-lists).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Minending: Adds an object to a generated mine at its entrance, along a tunnel or in a chamber. Use these entries for equipment and decoration that should follow the mine layout.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Minenspec: Requests mines associated with a district and its buildings. The settings control tunnel dimensions, branching, chambers, supports and ore. Placement requires suitable rock near the district.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_PawnListDef: Provides weighted pawn kinds for garrisons, spawn anchors, animal pens and container occupants. Spawn anchors also use the list role and radius. Garrisons and spawn anchors apply the settlement tech filter; pens and containers draw without that filter. See [Pawn lists](Modding-Pawns#pawn-lists).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_PawnListEntry: Adds one PawnKindDef to a pawn list, with a relative selection weight and an optional Ideology specialist role. Gear-based tech filtering and faction unit swaps can further affect which pawn is generated.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_PieceCategoryDef: Groups interchangeable pieces and supplies their shared placement rules. A plan can request the category instead of naming one building, allowing different layouts to use different pieces. Unset rules can inherit from parent categories; blockMax and merge are read from the primary category itself. See [Categories](Categories).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_PieceDef: Stores a building, wall segment or other reusable structure as character grids and a shared legend. Categories determine where the piece can be selected; anchors add variable furniture, loot, pawns and connections. See [Pieces and categories in XML](Modding-Pieces).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_RuinDef: Applies damage and occupation rules to a generated settlement. Quest sites use it for raided or occupied settlements, scenarios use it for a starting ruin the player moves into. It can create breaches, fire damage, collapsed roofs, overgrowth, corpses, prisoners and reduced loot. occupation determines whether the original faction, an occupier or nobody defends a quest site. See [Ruins](Modding-Overview#ruins) and [Starting in a ruin](Modding-Scenarios).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_SettlementPlanDef: Defines the building programme for a settlement: its wards, districts, fortifications and defenders. The generator fits this programme to the terrain when it creates the map. A materialList is required. See [Settlement types in XML](Modding-Settlements) for a complete example.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Stadtteil: Defines one ward within SettlementPlanDef.wards: Town, Suburb or Rural. Each ward has its own buildings, surfaces and defenders, and can configure fortifications or obstacles outside its boundary. Use districts to organise buildings within the ward. See [Wards](Modding-Settlements#wards).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_StyleDef: Identifies a style used when selecting wall profiles, with an optional fallback style. Styles do not filter the available building pieces. Define construction materials in MaterialListDef and building selection through categories.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Tauscheintrag: Maps a source pawn kind or object to a replacement within a UnitSwapDef. Several targets for the same source form a weighted selection among the rules with the highest priority.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Techschritt: Associates a map generation step with its minimum faction tech level. Add entries to MapStepsDef.fromTechLevel. This setting controls map generation, not the tech filter used by pawn lists.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_TerrainWeight: Adds one terrain candidate to a material role terrainMix. Relative weights control the mix; unlike terrainChain, this list provides variation rather than an ordered fallback.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_UnitSwapDef: Replaces generic pawn kinds and objects with faction-specific alternatives. Rules are resolved separately for each source and faction, with higher priorities overriding lower ones. See [Unit swap](Modding-Pawns#unit-swap).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_Vorfeldspec: Places groups of 1×1 obstacle pieces outside a ward wall or boundary. Roads and gate approaches remain clear, and blocked cells are skipped. Add entries to Stadtteil.outworks; see [Outworks](Modding-Settlements#outworks).
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_WallEntry: Selects a piece or category for a ward wall, emplacement or gatehouse list. The enclosing list determines whether the entry describes repeated wall segments or a requested number of defensive structures.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_WallProfileDef: Defines a repeating wall cross section and optional tower and gatehouse pieces. Settlement styles select a profile; explicit wall lists can supply the wall pieces directly. See [Wall profiles](Modding-Overview#wall-profiles).
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Ackerspec_count: Requested number of fields of this specification.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Ackerspec_plants: Fallback plant ThingDef names, used when crops provides no usable plant. This is a list of names, not a piece grid.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_count: Requested number of buildings, sampled from the range. Placement depends on available space. During reference resolution, counts above 150 are capped at 150.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_lootTable: Default loot table for content zones in pieces selected by this entry. A content zone with its own resolved table takes precedence.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_piece: Specific PieceDef to request. Takes precedence when tag is also supplied.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_tag: PieceCategoryDef to select buildings from, including its descendant categories. This is the current category field for a building request; use piece to request a specific template.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_withIdeo: Allow the entry only if the owning ideoligion contains at least one listed meme or precept defName. Without an ideoligion, a non-empty list rejects the entry.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_requires: Piece or category defNames. The entry is only planned once at least `requiresCount` of them stand somewhere in the settlement (all districts, town, suburb and countryside). Each name counts once, however many buildings match it. Conditional entries are planned after the others; if the condition is never met, for example because a name does not exist or two entries require each other, the entry is left out without an error and the reason is written to the detail log. Count, minimum and priority only apply once the condition is met. In dungeon levels such an entry is left out.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_requiresCount: How many of the names in `requires` must be present. 1 means any one of them, the number of names means all of them.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_withoutIdeo: Reject the entry if the owning ideoligion contains any listed meme or precept defName.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_ContentZoneSpec_chance: Probability that this connected content zone is filled at all.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_ContentZoneSpec_count: Number of object placements requested in this connected content zone. Available space can reduce the number placed; values below 1 place nothing.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_ContentZoneSpec_lootTable: LootTableDef for this zone. Falls back to the building request lootTable if no table resolves here.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_ContentZoneSpec_symbol: Character identifying this zone in PieceDef.content. Separate connected regions with the same symbol are filled separately.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Dekospec_count: Requested number for a defenses entry. If unset, defensive placement uses max, then one; decor placement uses spacing and max.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Dekospec_piece: Specific PieceDef to place instead of selecting from tag.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Dekospec_objects: Object list with single things, such as lamps, barrels or carts, instead of a piece. Name exactly one of piece, tag or objects. Members whose mod is missing are left out.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Dekospec_weight: Weight against the other entries with the same placement. At each spot one entry is picked by weight, its spacing sets the gap to the next spot.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Dekospec_tag: PieceCategoryDef supplying decoration or defensive pieces. The piece is drawn by its placement weight.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_label: Display name of the district. Falls back to name when omitted.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_name: District identifier used to associate buildings, fields, pens and mines. Must be unique across all districts of the plan.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_prefCenter: Preference for placing this district near the settlement centre.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_prefGate: Preference for placing this district near a gate.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_prefMain: Preference for placing this district along the main road.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_prefWall: Preference for placing this district near the wall.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_FactionFlagDef_faction: FactionDef defName receiving this flag assignment.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_FactionFlagDef_objects: LootBuildingCategoryDef names supplying flag objects. The faction uses a consistent choice from its flag lists.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Garnisonseintrag_count: Number of pawns requested from this list for the ward.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Garnisonseintrag_list: PawnListDef supplying the garrison. A missing list leaves this entry empty.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Gehegespec_count: Requested number of pens of this specification.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Gehegespec_name: Name used to identify the pen specification in messages.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Gehegespec_plants: Fallback plant ThingDef names for the pen, used when crops provides no usable plant.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Gehegespec_terrain: TerrainDef name for the pen surface, not a character grid.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_HafenEintrag_count: Requested number of harbour buildings from this entry.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_HafenEintrag_piece: Specific harbour PieceDef; takes precedence over tag.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_chance: Placement probability from 0 to 1. Object cells are checked individually; Fill, Object and Spawn anchors are checked as anchor regions.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_descentChance: Only with descentPlans. Chance that the descent exists. On a StairsDown anchor it is rolled when the settlement is built, on an object anchor when the container is opened.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_descentPlans: Dungeon plans this anchor may lead into, one is picked at random. On a StairsDown anchor in a settlement piece (cellar, graveyard entrance) a descent stairs is placed that leads into the first level of the picked plan. On an object anchor (sarcophagus, coffin) the opened container turns into a descent of the same size and keeps its empty look. The map below is only made when a pawn goes down. Without descentPlans, StairsDown keeps leading to the next level of the dungeon.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_lootTable: LootTableDef used by a Fill anchor. A selected object-list member can override it. Object anchors do not use the anchor loot table.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_pawnCount: Number of pawns requested by a Spawn anchor, sampled from this range. The spawn path treats values below 1 as 1.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_pawnList: PawnListDef used by a Spawn anchor. The list supplies pawn kinds, behaviour and radius, subject to the settlement tech filter.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_role: Construction role resolved through the settlement material list when the entry does not specify a concrete object or terrain. This is unrelated to pawn-list behaviour roles.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_roof: RoofDef placed when this symbol is used in the roof grid.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_terrain: TerrainDef placed when this symbol is used in the terrain grid.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_thing: ThingDef placed for this legend symbol in an object layer.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendVariant_stuff: Material for the alternative object. If omitted, the parent legend entry material is retained.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendVariant_terrain: Alternative TerrainDef for this legend entry.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendVariant_thing: Alternative ThingDef for this legend entry.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_chance: Probability that this entry is taken from always. Ignored when the entry is in the weighted entries list.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_count: Item quantity sampled from this range, then multiplied by countOverDepth if present. The resulting quantity is clamped to at least 1; use chance or weight to suppress an entry. Does not control nested tables.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_depthRange: Eligible depth interval for weighted entries. Settlements use depth 0. In always, the current implementation only applies this rejection when weightOverDepth is present.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_onMissing: Fallback for a missing direct thing: Skip omits it, Fallback tries fallbackThings in order, Silver substitutes Silver with the entry quantity. Silver is not a market-value conversion.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_stuff: Material for a direct thing result. Category results choose a suitable material randomly instead.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_table: Nested LootTableDef, evaluated tableRolls times. Takes precedence over category and thing; count does not multiply nested results.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_tableRolls: Number of evaluations of a nested table. Applies only when table resolves.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_thing: ThingDef name for a direct item result. Missing items are handled by onMissing.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_weight: Relative selection weight in entries. Zero excludes the entry unless weightOverDepth supplies a positive replacement weight. This is not a probability.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_weightOverDepth: Curve whose value replaces weight at the supplied depth. Settlements use depth 0.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootEntry_weightOverWealth: Curve multiplying the selection weight by the supplied wealth value. Normal settlement loot uses player-home wealth.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootTableDef_always: Entries evaluated before weighted draws, each with its own chance. They do not consume rolls and are not limited by maxEntriesPerResolve.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootTableDef_emptyFallback: LootTableDef evaluated if the entire result is empty. Cannot refer directly to this table. Nested and fallback evaluations share the recursion limit.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootTableDef_maxEntriesPer: Threshold checked before each weighted draw. Counts LootPick records, not individual items or final stacks. always entries and a nested-table result can exceed this threshold.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootTableDef_rollChance: One probability check for the entire weighted-draw phase. Does not suppress always entries; an empty result can still invoke emptyFallback.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootTableDef_uniqueEntries: Prevents selecting the same entry again during this table evaluation. Different entries and nested tables can still produce the same item.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_MaterialRole_chain: Ordered ThingDef names for this role. The first available candidate is selected; this is an object fallback list, not a category inheritance chain.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_MaterialRole_role: Construction role name used by the generator or a piece legend, for example WALL or DOOR. Use the established role identifiers documented in the material-list guide.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Minenspec_count: Requested number of mines associated with this specification.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Minenspec_tags: Building categories used to locate mine entrances near suitable district buildings.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PawnListDef_members: Weighted pawn kinds available to this list. Members whose PawnKindDef is unavailable are skipped.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PawnListDef_role: Behaviour for pawns spawned at piece anchors: Guard joins ward defence; Sentry holds a post; Gunner mans artillery. Civilian from older files counts as Guard. Garrison positioning is controlled by its post instead. Pens and container occupants have their own behaviour.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceDef_anchors: Character grid for Connect, Fill, Object and Spawn anchors. Each non-empty symbol refers to a legend entry; the entry determines what happens in that area.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceDef_content: Legacy character grid for content zones. Matching contentZones entries control object placement and loot.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceDef_style: Legacy style reference. Building selection is controlled by categories and placement rules.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceDef_type: Building, WallPart or DungeonRoom. The dungeon room type is used by dungeon rooms; see [Dungeon levels](Modding-Dungeons).
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PlacementRules_countPerSet: Legacy field retained in the data model. No current generation code reads it; request building quantities through district BudgetEntry.count instead.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_budget: Legacy building requests. Converted to a Default district only when neither top-level nor ward districts exist. Prefer wards and their districts for new plans.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_district: Legacy top-level district definitions. Prefer districts inside wards to make the intended ward explicit.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_factionT: FactionDef defNames or faction categoryTag values that explicitly qualify for this plan. Explicit matches take precedence over general tech-level plans.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_mapSize: Requested map edge length in cells. The map uses the larger of this value and the world map-size setting. Values below 150 are configuration errors.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_material: Required MaterialListDef supplying construction roles. A missing reference disables the plan.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_maxBuild: Legacy maximum-gap input. Prefer buildingGap on each ward; the current planner primarily uses the minimum gap.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_minBuild: Legacy minimum-gap input. Zero uses the compatibility default. Prefer buildingGap on the ward.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_roadLane: Side-lane width in cells, with the same limits as roadMain.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_roadMain: Main road width in cells. Maximum 6 for ModernTown and 2 for other supported kinds.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_share: Relative selection weight among eligible plans. Values of zero or less are treated as 1.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_style: Single-style compatibility field, used if styles is empty. Styles select wall profiles, not building categories.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_styles: Styles available for wall-profile selection. Does not restrict building pieces or replace the required materialList.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_targetBu: Target building coverage used to size and fill the settlement. Zero leaves the planner default in effect; see the settlement guide for tuning.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Stadtteil_districts: Districts belonging to this ward, each with building requests and optional fields, pens or mines.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Stadtteil_label: Display name of this ward. Does not rename the settlement on the world map.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Stadtteil_name: Internal ward name, normalised from kind during loading. Use label for the visible name.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Stadtteil_outworks: Groups of 1×1 obstacle pieces placed outside the ward boundary. Use distance, spacing, run and gateClearance on each Vorfeldspec to control placement.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_StyleDef_fallback: Next style tried in the style fallback chain. Circular chains are configuration errors.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_TerrainWeight_terrain: TerrainDef name used as one candidate in terrainMix.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Vorfeldspec_distance: Distance outside the wall or ward boundary in orthogonal cell steps. Values below 1 are treated as 1.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Vorfeldspec_gateClearance: Clearance around gate cells. Negative values are treated as zero. Roads, squares and fence gates also keep a one-cell clearance.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Vorfeldspec_piece: Specific 1×1 PieceDef used as the obstacle. Takes precedence over tag.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Vorfeldspec_run: Number of candidate cells attempted per group. Blocked cells are skipped, so the resulting group can contain fewer obstacles.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Vorfeldspec_tag: PieceCategoryDef supplying obstacle pieces. Candidates are selected uniformly; pieces larger than 1×1 are skipped.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_WallEntry_tag: PieceCategoryDef supplying pieces for this wall, emplacement or gatehouse entry. This is an active category selector.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_WallEntry_name: Internal compatibility name populated from a text entry or from piece/tag by the custom XML loader. A name element is not read; write piece or tag instead.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_WallEntry_count: Requested quantity for emplacements or gatehouses. Wall strips use weight and repeat along the boundary. Dungeon entrance and stairsDown lists currently turn each entry into one room request, regardless of this count.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_WallEntry_piece: Specific PieceDef selected by this entry. The custom loader also accepts a category name through the compatibility notation; prefer tag for a category.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Minending_list: LootBuildingCategoryDef supplying the mine object instead of a fixed thing. This is an object list, not a pawn list.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Minending_count: Requested number of these objects in the mine.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Minending_thing: ThingDef placed at the selected mine location.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_Minending_stuff: Material for the mine object when it is made from stuff.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_TerrainWeight_weight: Relative weight within terrainMix. The current resolver treats values of zero or less as 0.001, so remove an entry to exclude that terrain.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_factions: FactionDef names allowed to use pieces of this category. An unset list can inherit from parent categories.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_excludeFa: FactionDef names excluded from pieces of this category, subject to the piece/category rule precedence.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_openAcces: True makes pieces of this category enterable from every side, like markets, farms, landmarks and defensive positions. Inherits through parent categories; defaults to false.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_wallPart: Marks the category as part of the town wall: Segment, Tower or Gatehouse, or Attachment for pieces built onto the wall such as stairs to the walkway. The planner places Segment, Tower and Gatehouse with the fortification; the settlement check does not treat any of them as ordinary buildings. Inherits through parent categories; empty means not a wall part.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_EaveFamilyDef: Names the eave objects that CBF places around buildings when Architecture of the Rim is active: a straight eave and its outer and inner corner, chosen by the stuff categories of the wall material. The family marked fallback is used for any other material.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_EaveFamilyDef_straight: defName of the straight eave piece.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_EaveFamilyDef_outerCorner: defName of the outer corner eave piece.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_EaveFamilyDef_innerCorner: defName of the inner corner eave piece.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_EaveFamilyDef_stuffCategor: Stuff categories of the wall material for which this family is used, for example Stony or Woody.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_EaveFamilyDef_fallback: True uses this family for wall materials that no other family lists. One family should have it.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_farmhouse: True lets pieces of this category stand on farm plots when the settlement type names no farm categories of its own. Set on HouseSmall and Farm.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_pieceType: Piece type the editor gives new pieces of this category: Building, WallPart or DungeonRoom.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_dungeonPa: Marks the category as a dungeon part: Corridor, Entrance or Stairs. The dungeon editor offers its pieces in the matching lists. Inherits through parent categories.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_wallAcces: Connects pieces of this category to the wall walkway by adding access doors and closing exposed sides away from the wall. Inherits through parent categories; defaults to false.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_annexCorn: For annexes: opens the two house-wall corner cells at the ends of the attachment as floor. Useful for lean-to tents. Inherits through parent categories; defaults to false.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootMember_thing: ThingDef for the object placed at the anchor.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LootMember_lootTable: Member-specific LootTableDef overriding the anchor table. If it cannot be resolved, the anchor table is used.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonProfileDef_mapSize: Older profile map-size field. Set the surface size on SettlementPlanDef and lower-map sizes on DungeonLevel.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonProfileDef_style: Older profile style reference. Current dungeon plans use SettlementPlanDef; this profile is not selected by the level workflow.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_PlacementRules: Overrides supported category rules for one PieceDef, including selection weight, wall preference, faction restrictions and ideoligion conditions. Some legacy fields still load but are not read by the current planner; these are identified below.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PlacementRules_needsRoadAc: Legacy piece-level field. The current planner reads the open-access condition from categories, not this override.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PlacementRules_zones: Legacy piece-level field. For open access, set Outside together with needsRoadAccess=false on a category directly assigned to the piece. This piece-level list is not read by the current planner.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_zones: Outside together with needsRoadAccess=false enables open access. The current check reads categories directly assigned to the piece, not their parent chain. Inside and Center have no effect.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_needsRoad: Set false together with zones containing Outside to enable open access. That combination is checked on categories directly assigned to the piece. District preferences determine location.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_siteTags: Eligibility tags for automatic quest-site plan selection. Empty excludes the plan from that pool. A fixed usable plan supplied by the site extension or quest node bypasses tag selection.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_required: Retained anchor flag, also used by editor validation for missing anchor cells. It does not force wall placement. Set placement/atWall to Required on the piece for that behaviour.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_symbol: One character identifying this entry in the piece grids. Symbols are case-sensitive: a and A are different entries. Write exactly one character; longer values are invalid.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_anchor: Anchor name. Wall, Outside, Annex, NoShare (no shared wall on these wall cells) and Water have settlement connection meanings. Dungeon stairs use StairsUp and StairsDown. Other names identify furniture, loot or pawn areas, for example Kitchen. Draw the entry symbol in anchors or anchorsOver.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_stuff: Material for the concrete thing in this legend entry. It must be valid stuff for that ThingDef; missing or incompatible stuff falls back to the default material. Variants have their own material field.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_MaterialRole_district: Ward condition: Town, Suburb or Rural. Despite the field name, this selects a ward, not a named DistrictSpec. During settlement generation it also applies when a piece resolves a material role at that location.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_MaterialRole_forPieces: Piece or category names matched against the ward's fortification pieces. This is a condition on the ward context, not a filter selecting the individual house being stamped. A matching row outranks a ward-only row.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_PieceCategoryDef_parent: Another PieceCategoryDef whose members include this category's pieces. Unset inheritable rules are read along this chain. This runtime link uses a defName and is separate from RimWorld XML ParentName inheritance.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_MaterialListDef_parent: Fallback MaterialListDef. CBF first looks for a usable matching role in this list, then searches the parent. Use a child list to change selected construction roles without duplicating the others.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_DungeonLevel: One level in a dungeon plan. Its districts request rooms, its garrison supplies defenders, and its stair-room lists connect it to adjacent maps. See [Dungeon levels](Modding-Dungeons). The shipped dungeons of the Medieval Overhaul set are good examples.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_SpreadEntry: Record intended to distribute room requests across dungeon levels; not used by the generator yet. It is saved and validated but is not consumed by the current framework-to-planner conversion. Use entries in each level's districts for working room requests.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_name: Internal name of this level. Used as its label when label is empty.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_label: Display name of this level in the editor. Empty uses name.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_layout: Level layout: Corridors, Chambers, Cave, Rows, Grid, Temple or Warren. Grid sets the rooms on a loose grid with thick rock between them, joined by straight passages and cross links. Temple puts the largest room in the middle with long axis passages, rooms in pairs and side niches. Warren lets the rooms share their walls. Rows lays a main corridor with a few bends and puts the rooms in rows along both sides. A district can override it with its own layout field.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_districts: Room groups for this level. Each district contains category or piece requests in entries.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_garrison: Defenders requested for this level, using pawn lists, counts and posts.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_entrance: Stair-room pieces or categories for arrival from the level above. Used on lower levels only. Each list entry becomes one room request; mark its portal cell with a StairsUp Connect anchor.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_stairsDown: Stair-room pieces or categories leading to the next level. Required on every level except the last. Each list entry becomes one room request; mark its portal cell with a StairsDown Connect anchor.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_corridors: Corridor pieces or categories, such as torches, candles, bones or runners. The generator dresses the corridors of this level with them, picked by weight. A section with its own `corridors` uses those instead.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_mapSize: Lower-level pocket-map edge length in cells. A positive value is used directly; 0 estimates the size from the room requests. The first level uses the surface map, so set that size on the plan.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_caveWidth: Width of the cave paths in cells, rolled per cell from this range, 1 to 5.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_caveShare: Share of the connections between districts that are dug as winding cave paths instead of straight masoned corridors, 0 to 1. At 0 a cave path is only made when a district finds no other connection. Cave-to-cave links always stay cave paths.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_secretChance: Chance that a room door, which would otherwise be bricked up, gets a narrow secret passage through the rock to the nearest corridor or to the door of another room. The door becomes a secret door (material list role DOOR_SECRET). At most this share of the rooms gets one. 0 turns secret passages off.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_socketType: Socket connector kind: Door, Arch, Cave or Secret. Stored by the editor but not used by the generator yet; it does not create a working connection by itself.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_socketWidth: Socket width, default 1. Stored by the editor but not used by the generator yet.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_mountain: Minimum rock thickness of the mountain over old town and suburb, 0 to 16. 0 means no mountain, except for MountainCity, which then uses 4. Fields inside the mountain are dark; the plan check names plants that do not grow there.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_levels: Ordered dungeon levels, starting at the surface. Used when kind is Dungeon. Every non-final level requires stairsDown; see [Dungeon levels](Modding-Dungeons).
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_spread: Stored requests intended to span several levels. The current planner conversion does not consume this list. Put room requests in levels/li/districts instead.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_layouts: List of layouts the level may use, for example Chambers, Temple and Grid. Each generated level picks one of them from its seed, so the same plan looks different from site to site, like coreShapes for an old town. When the list is set, it replaces layout. Districts without their own layout follow the picked one.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_layouts: Optional list of layouts for this district. The district picks one of them from the seed. When the list is set, it replaces layout. Prefer the list on the level so that a level keeps one look.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_count: Requested number of buildings, sampled from the range. Placement depends on available space. During reference resolution, counts above 150 are capped at 150.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_lootTable: Default loot table for content zones in pieces selected by this entry. A content zone with its own resolved table takes precedence.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_piece: Specific PieceDef to request. Takes precedence when tag is also supplied.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_tag: PieceCategoryDef to select buildings from, including its descendant categories. This is the current category field for a building request; use piece to request a specific template.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_withIdeo: Allow the entry only if the owning ideoligion contains at least one listed meme or precept defName. Without an ideoligion, a non-empty list rejects the entry.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_requires: Same as on BudgetEntry. The spread list is not applied by the current planner conversion.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_requiresCount: How many of the names in `requires` must be present. 1 means any one of them, the number of names means all of them.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_withoutIdeo: Reject the entry if the owning ideoligion contains any listed meme or precept defName.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_WallProfileDef_style: StyleDef used to select this wall profile for a settlement. It does not select house categories or replace the plan's materialList.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_RuinDef_overgrowth: Chance per open cell of the settlement that a wild plant of the biome grows there, 0 to 1, scaled by the plant density of the biome (deserts get little, extreme deserts none). Makes a settlement look long abandoned.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_RuinDef_overgrowthTrees: Share of the overgrowth plants that are trees instead of bushes, 0 to 1.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_RuinDef_townWallDecay: Share of the town wall that has fallen down, 0 to 1. The gaps come in short stretches.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_RuinDef_roofCollapse: How likely the roof of a room has caved in, 0 to 1, more often near the attack. A collapsed roof covers 40 to 100 % of the room.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_RuinDef_lightsOut: true empties all fuel and switches off everything that can be switched, so torches and lamps are out.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_DungeonSection: One section of a dungeon level, for example the entrance or the back part. Each section has its own districts and can have its own corridor dressing. The stairs up are placed in the first section, the stairs down in the last.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_BudgetEntry_priority: Which entry gets space first. With equal priority the previous order applies (minimum count, size). Low entries may stay below their minimum when space runs out. Not used in dungeon areas.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_count: How many times this level is built in a row, 1 to 20.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonLevel_sections: Parts of the level, for example Entrance and Back, each with its own districts and corridors. The stairs up are in the first section, the stairs down in the last. Without sections the level uses its own `districts` and `corridors`.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonSection_corridors: Corridor pieces or categories for this section. Empty uses the corridors of the level.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DungeonSection_label: Display name in the editor. Empty uses name.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_annexCategorie: Only on an Annex anchor. The annex at this anchor is taken from these categories. Empty means the annexes set at the category of the piece.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_annexPriority: Only on an Annex anchor. Anchors with a higher priority get their annex first. Critical and Important ignore annexChance, Preferred raises it, Low halves it. Low anchors are filled last, after all other annexes of the settlement. annexRequired is independent and stronger.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_annexRequired: Only on an Annex anchor. The piece is only placed if an annex fits at this anchor.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_biomes: BiomeDef defNames. The type is only used on tiles with one of these biomes. Unknown names, for example from mods that are not loaded, are ignored.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_hillines: The type is only used on tiles with one of these hilliness values. Empty means any.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_landform: TileMutatorDef defNames, for example River, Coast, Lake or Odyssey landforms. The type is only used on tiles that have at least one of them.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_maxCivil: Only for older pawn lists with role Civilian, which now count as Guard: limits how many anchors with such lists get pawns. 0 means no limit.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_notBiome: BiomeDef defNames. The type is never used on tiles with one of these biomes.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_notLandf: TileMutatorDef defNames. The type is never used on tiles that have one of them.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_ruin: Builds every settlement of this type as a ruin, with the damage, overgrowth, corpses and loot rules of the RuinDef. With `occupation` Builder the owning faction still lives there. A ruin set by a quest or site takes precedence. CBF ships `CBF_Ruin_Plundered` (little loot) and `CBF_Ruin_Unplundered` (loot stays), both with the owners still living there.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_suburbRi: Only for a suburb wall with a walkway (depth 3 or more). true: the suburb becomes a closed ring around the town. false: the suburb stays as separate areas on the sides, as many as suburbIslands allows; with suburbIslands 0 the ring stays.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_withIdeo: Meme or precept defNames, for example `Tunneler`. The type is only used for a faction whose primary ideoligion has at least one of them. Without the Ideology DLC the condition is ignored and only tags and tech levels decide.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SettlementPlanDef_withoutI: Meme or precept defNames. The type is never used for a faction whose primary ideoligion has one of them. Ignored without the Ideology DLC.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_UnitSwapDef_neutral: Older field. It is still loaded but no longer protects pawn kinds from the swap.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_UnitSwapDef_units: Pawn kind replacements for this faction, each entry swaps the kind in from for the kind in to. Humanlike kinds without a rule that the faction does not use are swapped for one of its own kinds. If the faction has no fitting kind, the place stays empty.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_FloorListDef_floors: The floors of this list, each with a weight. Each time the list is used one floor is drawn by weight. Floors from mods that are not loaded are skipped; if none is left, pieces keep their own floor.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_FloorListEntry_materialFro: If true, the floor is adapted to the stone of the map, for example stone tiles in the rock type found there. Do not combine with materials.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_FloorListEntry_materials: Optional variants of this floor (TerrainDef defNames), for example several wood types. One of them is picked at random. Ignored when materialFromMap is true.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_floorList: A FloorListDef (defName) for this floor symbol. Instead of the entry's own terrain, a floor is drawn from the list. If the list has no usable floor, the own terrain is used.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LegendEntry_floorPerCell: Only with floorList. true: every cell of this symbol draws its own floor, giving a mixed floor. false: one floor is drawn for the whole piece.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_RuinDef_creatures: A PawnListDef whose creatures occupy the ruin instead of the usual defenders, for example insects or undead. Pawns of a faction defend a point together, animals without a faction turn manhunter. Empty uses the occupation setting.
LanguageData.CBF_DefDesc_LandmarkPlanDef: Turns a settlement plan into an Odyssey landmark on the world map. When a map is generated on such a tile, CBF builds the plan there, usually as a ruin, in the building style of a matching faction. Needs Odyssey; without it nothing is created.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_plan: The settlement plan built on the landmark tile. Required.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_ruin: Optional RuinDef applied after building, for damage, overgrowth and corpses. Empty builds the place intact.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_commonalit: How often the landmark appears compared with other landmarks. Must be above 0.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_nameMaker: RulePackDef for the landmark name. Empty uses the name maker of vanilla ruin landmarks.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_icon: Texture path of the world map icon. Empty uses the vanilla ruins icon.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_styleFacti: FactionDef whose building style is used. Empty picks a faction of the plan's tech level, or any faction with CBF settlement types.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_loot: If false, the landmark is built without loot.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_biomes: BiomeDefs the landmark may appear in. Empty means all biomes.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_biomesExcl: BiomeDefs the landmark never appears in.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_coast: Egal: coast does not matter. Pflicht: only on coast tiles. Nie: never on coast tiles.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_LandmarkPlanDef_river: Egal: river does not matter. Pflicht: only on tiles with a river. Nie: never on tiles with a river.
